Package hadur2.core.port

package hadur2.core.port
The core's outbound ports: the only ways it reaches anything outside plain computation.
  • Telemetry takes the core's CSV records (V, B, EW, P, MEM, FAULT, R, M). The robot prints them; tests and the bench collect them.
  • ProfileStore holds opponent profiles between battles as named byte blobs under a quota. It is deliberately dumb: the memory package's ProfileLibrary owns the format, the checksums, crash-safe replacement (RES-3), eviction (MEM-5) and turning storage failures into an empty profile (MEM-4).
  • MemoryProfileStore is the in-memory store for tests and the bench; it can cut a write short at any byte, so RES-3 is tested without files. The file-backed adapter, hadur2.FileProfileStore, lives in the robot module, because it needs Robocode's data directory and file I/O.

Ports exist so the core keeps its rules: no robocode.* (CORE-1) and no I/O or clock (RES-6) inside the core, with the adapter supplying the real implementations. ArchUnit (ArchitectureTest) forbids this package to depend on the gun, movement or replay packages; it uses nothing beyond java.util. Opponent memory reaches storage only through ProfileStore (the rule tagged MEM-3).
